description: F-CORE-031: a journal read that is both cheap and lossless. The plainest view a bookkeeping application has had two bad ways to be filled. `journalExport` is lossless and builds five streams with a SHA-256 each, has no date window and no paging — an archive format answering a list view's question, paid for on every page load. `datevExport` has the window and the weight but is DATEV-shaped and therefore LOSSY FOR SPLIT ENTRIES: an expense with its input tax against one bank line collapses into a single row and the tax line disappears, so a journal view built on it would quietly hide every tax line in the books. This projection is datevExport's cost with journalExport's completeness: every line of every entry, account numbers AND names resolved, no hashes. Paging counts ENTRIES rather than lines, because a page boundary falling inside a split entry would reproduce exactly the defect the projection exists to avoid; `count` is the number of entries in the window before paging, so a page header can name the total without a second call that costs an export. Ordered by sequenceNumber, the journal's own total order — paging needs a stable one and the ledger already has it.

expect.comment: The split entry from the finding: three lines, and DATEV's one row per entry cannot carry them.
All three entries, the split one with all three of its lines, each account with its name. No window, no paging: count and the list agree.
The date window journalExport does not have. count follows the window, not the year.

Paging: one entry from the second, and `count` still names all three so a page header does not need a second call. Never one LINE from the second — a page boundary inside a split entry is the defect this projection avoids.
Past the end is an empty page, not an error: a caller paging forward finds out by getting nothing.
